checks: Integral midpoint fibers force all selected positive q-direction spaces to coincide. Projecting to that space is an isometry on each involved affine plane. Brunn–Minkowski gives both anchored roof data inequalities and actual midpoint lower bounds in dimension q.

The maximum average of input roots over the compact representation polytope is finite and concave and agrees with each datum. The projected upper-face subdivision covers the hull and the roof is affine on each cell. A common pulling order agrees on cell faces. Stellar insertion introduces exactly the remaining selected points while subdividing all incident simplices compatibly and preserving their affine pieces.

The maximizer set is convex and a subcomplex with connected graph. On an initial segment toward a maximizing point a nonmaximal vertex lies in an incident simplex and the affine roof must have a strictly higher vertex there. One such ascending parent per nonmaximal vertex, with a rooted tree on the maximizing subgraph, reaches the root from every vertex and gives a spanning tree.

The midpoint of each edge is integral and in its relative interior. Distinct triangulation edges have disjoint relative interiors and no selected vertex there, so the corresponding actual fibers are counted once. For parent b≥c the tree bound uses δb+(1−δ)c with δ=2^(−q) by the binomial expansion. For non-tree edges the two pure terms give δ(w_p+w_p').

After removing M_P−a from the tree child baselines, the root coefficient is deg(p_*) and every other coefficient is deg(p)−2. Every vertex has degree at least s, hence the stated rank bound and sδa. The path and singleton cases give the claimed expressions directly.

For the sharp example the affine positive radius gives a convex fibered body. Its only integer bases are 0, 2e_i, e_i, e_i+e_j. The selected all-even volumes are 1 and s copies of b=ε^q. The other volumes are s copies of c=((1+ε)/2)^q and binom(s,2) copies of b. The exact excess is s(c−b)+binom(s,2)b, tending to s2^(−q). The embedding in a q-plane and optional base thickening leave the counted fibers unchanged.

Original 670310a99fe94843 §§1–4 gives the same graph inequality, cap scope and sharpness. Its intrinsic direction reference is internalized by the first paragraph, including the dimension bound for a closed cap taken on its own.

overlap.comparison: Uses a triangulation to avoid midpoint collisions, but proves a different weighted amplification bound under an extra smaller-rank weight-spread condition. The present ascending roof and degree bookkeeping do not require that condition.

Gives a level-integrated rank count for an entire residue in full dimension. It does not give this graph-dependent bound for any selected subset or the optimal additional term proportional to the peak.
Covers the direction-space step for intrinsic midpoint geometry. The graph, degree estimate, sharpness family and application to a compact cap are separate.

readability: The triangulation is of the selected support and roof, so a midpoint outside its vertex set may still lie in the same parity class. It contributes an uncounted actual fiber in either case.
review_method: Independent cold read of the frozen proof, then original-source and accepted-predecessor comparison.
summary: The intrinsic concave roof gives a conforming ascending triangulation. Its distinct integer edge midpoints give the exact degree estimate and the optimal rank coefficient.
